title: Georgekutty Walks Into 200 Countries at Once. Drishyam 3 Lands on Prime Video and the Diaspora Finally Gets the Twist Everyone's Been Whispering About.
excerpt: Mohanlal's ₹330-crore Malayalam juggernaut hits Amazon Prime Video in four languages worldwide — the OTT drop the NRI WhatsApp groups have been counting down to.
body:
There is a particular silence that falls over a desi living room when Georgekutty starts thinking. You can almost hear the man's mind working behind those tired eyes — the schoolteacher's son who never finished fourth grade and yet keeps outwitting the entire Kerala police force. As of June 18, that silence belongs to your sofa. **Drishyam 3** is streaming on **Amazon Prime Video**, and for the millions of Malayalis, Tamils, Telugus and Kannadigas scattered from Sharjah to San Jose, the wait is finally, gloriously over.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=07h9Y1XKBWI</youtube>

Let's be honest about why this one matters more than the average OTT drop. The **Drishyam** franchise isn't a movie series — it's a thirteen-year-old family secret the whole subcontinent is in on. From the 2013 original to the 2021 sequel that broke lockdown viewing records, **Mohanlal**'s Georgekutty has become the most beloved everyman-criminal in Indian cinema: the father who buries a body and then buries the truth so deep that even the audience has to lean in. The third chapter, directed once again by the franchise's architect **Jeethu Joseph**, picks up roughly four and a half years after the second film left Georgekutty seemingly untouchable — and promptly starts pulling the rug out again.

It arrives on streaming carrying the weight of a genuine theatrical monster. Released worldwide on May 21 to coincide with Mohanlal's birthday, the film crossed ₹236 crore globally and was declared the highest-grossing Malayalam film of the year, with the makers trumpeting a combined gross-and-business figure of ₹330 crore. That is not a regional success. That is a Mollywood film muscling into the conversation usually reserved for the big-budget Hindi and Telugu tentpoles.

> "What began as a story rooted in Kerala eventually travelled across multiple languages and regions, connecting with audiences beyond its original market." — the makers, marking the film's 25th day in cinemas

And here is where the diaspora angle turns from nice-to-have into the whole point. Prime Video didn't just buy the streaming rights — it went to the **Delhi High Court** to protect them, securing interim relief that restrained the makers from cutting side deals on the franchise. That is how badly Amazon wanted Georgekutty in its library. The payoff for viewers abroad is the kind of access that used to be a fantasy: the film is streaming exclusively in **Malayalam with dubbed versions in Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**, available to Prime members across India and more than 200 countries and territories. No grainy pirated link at 3 a.m., no waiting for a relative to send a pen drive. If you have Prime, Georgekutty is sitting in your queue tonight, wherever you are.

The craft, mercifully, has not been diluted for the small screen. Joseph reunites the core ensemble — **Meena** as the steadfast Rani, **Ansiba Hassan** and **Esther Anil** back as daughters Anju and Anu, with **Siddique**, **Asha Sarath**, Murali Gopy and Kalabhavan Shajon rounding out a cast that knows exactly how this slow-burn machine works. Satheesh Kurup's cinematography keeps the Thodupuzha hill country looking lush and faintly menacing, and Anil Johnson's score does that thing the franchise has perfected: stretching ordinary domestic moments until they hum with dread. The plot, as ever, hinges on a fresh investigation reopening old wounds, and on a man who has convinced himself — and his family — that they have finally outrun the system. They have not. They never do. That's the contract, and Joseph honours it with a couple of twists that have kept the Mollywood internet in delicious knots since May.

Is it the best of the three? The diehards will argue that forever, and that argument is half the fun. But there's no debate about what this release represents: a Malayalam suspense drama, with no item numbers and no pan-India marketing machine, becoming a genuine global event purely on the strength of writing and a 65-year-old superstar who can hold a frame with a single, unreadable glance.

So clear the evening. Put the phone face-down. Tell the family the climax of *Drishyam 2* was nothing. Georgekutty has one more move, and for the first time, the entire diaspora gets to watch him make it at the exact same moment as Kerala. Streaming now on Prime Video — pick your language and try, just try, to outguess him.
